title: Partnership Strategy
summary: Why partnerships beat cold email. 30+ specific targets for AOM growth.
content:
Partnership Strategy Brief

Date: 2026-03-10 Agent: Alex (Deal Architect) Purpose: Specific, actionable partnership targets for AOM to grow construction retainers and adjacent revenue. Built so Jacob can start reaching out.

Why Partnerships Beat Cold Email

Cold email = "Let me sell you something." Partnership outreach = "We both serve the same people. Let's make each other look good."

Construction is a handshake industry. The council confirmed cold email alone gets ~1 deal/month. Partnerships compress that timeline because you're borrowing trust someone else already built. A referral from a contractor's CPA carries more weight than 50 cold emails.

1. Partnership Categories (Ranked by Potential)

TIER 1: Already Have the Relationship + Ready to Refer

A. Construction CPAs and Bookkeepers

Why they'd partner with AOM: Their clients ask them for business advice constantly. When a contractor says "I need more jobs," the CPA has no answer. AOM gives them one. It makes the CPA look like a strategic advisor, not just a tax guy.

What AOM offers them: A trusted referral for their clients' marketing needs. Co-branded "grow your construction business" content. Reciprocal referrals (AOM's clients need construction-savvy CPAs too).

What they offer AOM: Direct introductions to contractors who trust them with their financials. These are warm leads with budget (if they have a CPA, they're doing real revenue).

Specific targets in Phoenix:

Firm Why Target Them Contact Approach
Whyte CPA (whytecpapc.com) Specializes in HVAC, electrical, plumbing, GC accounting. Talks about helping contractors "scale profitably." Perfect alignment. Email the founder directly.
Sean Core CPA (seancorecpa.com) Dedicated contractor/construction CPA practice. Small firm = easier to reach the decision maker. Email or LinkedIn DM.
Conover Asay CPAs (conoverasay.com) Full construction accounting page. Serves GCs, subcontractors, construction management firms. Email the partner who runs the construction practice.
Wallace Plese + Dreher (wpdcpa.com) Mid-size firm, dedicated construction vertical across AZ. Certified QuickBooks ProAdvisors for contractors. Ask for an intro meeting with their construction practice lead.
Price Kong (pricekong.com) Construction Services Group with "extensive experience." Larger firm = more client referrals if you get in. Request a partnership meeting with the construction group head.

B. Construction Business Coaches

Why they'd partner with AOM: They coach contractors on growth, but they can't deliver the marketing themselves. Their clients keep asking "how do I get more visible?" and the coach has no execution partner. AOM fills that gap and makes the coaching program look more complete.

What AOM offers them: An execution partner for the marketing side of their growth plans. "When you tell your client to invest in marketing, send them to us." Client success stories = coaching program success stories.

What they offer AOM: Pre-qualified leads. A contractor working with a growth coach has already committed to spending money to grow. They have budget and intent.

Specific targets in Phoenix:

Firm Why Target Them Contact Approach
Waters Business Consulting (watersbusinessconsulting.com) Grew a construction company from $7.5M to $43M. They know the space and their clients need marketing support at that scale. Email founder. Reference their construction case study.
The Aspire Institute (theaspireinstitute.com) Dedicated contractor coaching practice in Phoenix. This is literally their only vertical. Partnership meeting. Propose becoming their recommended marketing vendor.
Action Coach of Arizona (actioncoachofaz.com) Has a specific construction coaching landing page. Targets construction professionals for "sustainable growth." LinkedIn + email.

C. Surety Bonding Agents

Why they'd partner with AOM: This is the niche play. Bonding agents see contractors at a pivotal growth moment: when they're trying to bid bigger projects and need bigger bonds. A contractor going from $500K jobs to $2M jobs NEEDS better marketing. The bonding agent can say "and here's who can help you look the part."

What AOM offers them: A referral for their clients who need to professionalize their image (website, social presence, brand) to win bigger contracts. Many GCs and project owners Google the sub before awarding work. A terrible website or zero social presence costs bids.

What they offer AOM: Introductions to contractors who are actively growing and have proven revenue (you don't get bonded without financials). These are quality leads.

Specific targets in Phoenix:

Firm Why Target Them Contact Approach
Constructors Bonding, Inc. (CBI) (cbialliance.com) Arizona's largest surety agents since 1981. Hundreds of contractor clients. One referral relationship here = ongoing pipeline. Request a meeting. Frame it as "your clients are growing, we help them look like it."
CCI Surety (ccisurety.com) Southwest Regional Office in Phoenix. Specializes in hard-to-place bonds, meaning they work with contractors in active growth mode. Email the Phoenix office.
Southwest Bond Services (bondwriter.com) 25+ years in AZ. Local, relationship-driven. Easier to build a personal connection. Phone call + follow-up email.

TIER 2: High Volume Access to Your Exact Customer

D. HVAC/Plumbing Supply Houses and Distributors

Why they'd partner with AOM: This is the "who already has their attention" play. Every mechanical contractor walks into a supply house multiple times a week. These distributors host contractor events, training days, product launches. They want to add value to their contractor customers beyond just selling parts.

What AOM offers them: Content for their contractor events (video recaps, social coverage). Co-branded educational content ("How to market your HVAC business" hosted at their showroom). Makes the supply house a hub, not just a warehouse.

What they offer AOM: Physical access to hundreds of contractors. Bulletin board placement. Event sponsorship or co-hosting. Introduction to their contractor customer base.

Specific targets in Phoenix:

Firm Why Target Them Contact Approach
Arizona Climate Supply (azclimatesupply.com) Local. Carries HVAC and plumbing. Hosts contractor-facing events. Has a Phoenix showroom. Visit in person. Propose co-hosting a "marketing for contractors" event.
Johnstone Supply Phoenix (johnstonesupply.com) Major HVAC distributor. Hosts training events. Franchised = local owner makes partnership decisions. Email or visit the Phoenix store manager.
HVAC Depot Arizona (hvacdepotaz.com) Arizona-focused wholesale. Smaller = easier to get a "yes" on a partnership. Email or phone. Propose a flyer/QR code in their showroom.
Central Arizona Supply (centralazsupply.com) Largest in-stock plumbing selection in Phoenix. Contractor customers in and out daily. Visit the showroom. Talk to the manager about a referral arrangement.

E. Construction Staffing Agencies

Why they'd partner with AOM: Staffing agencies are in a war for contractor clients. They're always looking for ways to differentiate. Offering "marketing support" as a value-add to their contractor clients makes them stickier.

What AOM offers them: Content partnership (case studies, LinkedIn content about workforce challenges). Referral relationship. Help them market themselves to contractors.

What they offer AOM: Introductions to contractor clients. Staffing agencies know exactly which contractors are growing (because they're hiring more workers).

Specific targets in Phoenix:

Firm Why Target Them Contact Approach
Trades Corp Arizona's premier construction staffing agency, Phoenix HQ. They know every growing contractor in the Valley. Email or LinkedIn. "Your clients are growing. We help them look like it."
Tradesmen International (tradesmeninternational.com) National brand, local Phoenix office. Larger network of contractor clients. Request a meeting with the Phoenix branch manager.
K5 Rental (k5rental.com) Family-owned equipment rental in the Valley. Personal relationships with contractors. Visit in person. Small company = faster partnership decisions.

F. Vehicle Wrap / Fleet Graphics Companies

Why they'd partner with AOM: A contractor who wraps their trucks is already investing in brand visibility. They've crossed the mental threshold of "marketing matters." But wraps are a one-time purchase. AOM offers the ongoing digital side.

What AOM offers them: Reciprocal referrals ("You did their trucks, we'll do their website and social"). Joint case studies. Help them with their own social media (most wrap shops have terrible Instagram).

What they offer AOM: Introductions to contractors who already spend on marketing. The lead quality is excellent because the intent is proven.

Specific targets in Phoenix:

Firm Why Target Them Contact Approach
1st Impressions Truck Lettering (1stimpressions.com) Central Phoenix since 1994. 30 years of contractor relationships. Visit the shop. Bring Ambition as a case study.
Fast-Trac Designs (fast-tracdesigns.com) Arizona's leading vehicle wrap provider since 2007. Works with commercial fleets. Email or visit. Propose a referral swap.
SmartWrap (smartwrap.com) Phoenix-based, does design + install. Likely serves construction fleets. LinkedIn or email.

TIER 3: Strategic Positioning Plays

G. Trade Associations (Event Partnerships)

Not for cold outreach. For showing up.

What AOM offers: Videography for events, member spotlight content, social media coverage. Offer to film one event for free (cost: your time). The footage becomes your demo reel AND gets you in front of every member.

What they offer AOM: Stage time, member directory access, credibility, and a room full of your target customer.

Specific targets:

Association Members Opportunity
Mechanical Trade Contractors of Arizona (MTCAZ) (mtcaz.org) HVAC/mechanical contractors across AZ Offer to film a training event or annual meeting. This is Ambition's exact peer group.
Arizona Builders Alliance (ABA) (azbuilders.org) 380+ commercial contractors Sponsor or film an event. Ask about affiliate membership.
SMACNA Arizona (smacna-az.org) Sheet metal and HVAC contractors Offer member spotlight video series.
American Subcontractors Association of AZ (ASA-AZ) (asa-az.org) Subcontractors across trades Propose a "Sub Spotlight" video series for their members.
NAIOP Arizona (naiopaz.org) 900+ commercial real estate professionals Higher-end. Good for corporate event production referrals.

Upcoming events to target:

  • MCAA Annual Convention (March 15-19, 2026, JW Marriott Phoenix Desert Ridge). Mechanical contractors convention. AOM's exact vertical. If there's any way to attend, film, or connect with attendees, this is the single highest-density opportunity in the next 30 days.
  • Advancing Construction Analytics (April 20-22, 2026, Phoenix). Tech-forward contractors. Good for AI advisory positioning.
  • AZAGC events (ongoing, check azagc.org/events). Regular networking and education events.

H. Construction Attorneys

Why they'd partner with AOM: Attorneys who serve contractors need referral relationships. When a contractor wins a big case or expands, the attorney can say "and here's who to call for your marketing." It's a professional referral network play.

Specific targets:

Firm Notes
Lang Thal King & Hanson (lang.law) #5 in AZ for construction litigation. Deep contractor relationships.
Righi Fitch Law Group (righilaw.com) Handles ROC complaints, mechanics liens. Sees contractors at stress points where they need to professionalize.
Holden Willits (holdenwillits.com) Best Lawyers 2026, Tier 1 in Phoenix for construction. Premium clients.

I. Construction Insurance Brokers

Why: Same logic as CPAs and bonding agents. Insurance brokers see every contractor's financials and growth trajectory. They're trusted advisors.

Specific targets:

Firm Notes
PJO Insurance Brokerage (pjobrokerage.com) Workers' comp for construction. Phoenix-based. Small firm, personal relationships.
Contractors Choice Agency (contractorschoiceagency.com) Construction insurance specialist, 20+ years. Phoenix and Chandler offices.
JP Insurance Group (jpinsurancegrp.com) Serves HVAC, electrical, plumbing contractors specifically in Phoenix Valley.

2. Niche / Outside-the-Box Ideas

These are the ones nobody else is doing.

A. "Film Their Supply House Event for Free"

Pick one supply house (Arizona Climate Supply or Johnstone Supply). Offer to film their next contractor training day or product launch event for free. You walk away with:

  • A highlight reel that shows your work
  • Face time with 30-50 contractors in one room
  • A relationship with the supply house
  • Content you can post on LinkedIn with construction hashtags

Cost: half a day of shooting. ROI: potentially multiple retainer clients.

B. Construction Podcast Guest Strategy

These local shows need guests. Patrik going on one episode reaches their entire audience of contractors.

  • Building Arizona (Apple Podcasts) - Interviews people who build Arizona. Patrik's story fits perfectly.
  • AZ ROC Talk Podcast (roc.az.gov) - The Registrar of Contractors' own podcast. Discusses workforce development, technology. AOM's AI angle is a fresh take.
  • Construction Hall of Fame Podcast - Hosted by Brad Leavitt of AFT Construction in Scottsdale. Spotlights industry leaders.
  • That Plumbing Podcast - Phoenix-based. If AOM is doing work for plumbing/mechanical contractors, this is relevant.

C. ROC Licensing Schools as Referral Partners

Arizona Contractor License Center (azclc.com) has been prepping contractors for licensing exams since 1983. Every student who passes becomes a newly licensed contractor who needs... a website and social media presence. This is a fresh business owner at day zero of needing marketing.

The play: Partner with AZCLC. "Congratulations on your license. Here's a special offer from AOM for your first website and social setup." Could be a flyer in their materials, a co-branded email, or a discount code.

D. Equipment Rental Companies

Contractors who rent equipment are actively working. The bigger they rent, the bigger their projects. Equipment rental companies know who's growing.

  • K5 Rental (k5rental.com) - Family-owned, Phoenix Valley. Personal relationships.
  • Apache Equipment Rentals (apacherentals.com) - Local since 2004. Serves the exact contractor profile.
  • Sunstate Equipment (sunstateequip.com) - Local since 1977. Deep Valley roots.

The play: Bulletin board flyer, co-hosted event, or simply a referral relationship with their sales team.

E. Construction Tech Companies

Innovative Construction Technology (ICT) and Punctual are Phoenix-based construction tech startups. They sell to the same contractors AOM targets. They need marketing themselves, and their contractor clients need marketing. Double play: serve them AND partner with them.

F. Safety Training Companies as Event Partners

  • P3 Safety Solutions (p3safetysolutions.com) - Phoenix-based, trains construction crews
  • OSHA Phoenix LLC (phoenixoshatraining.com) - Trains in English and Spanish
  • Safirst Safety Consulting (safirst.com) - Construction safety veterans

These companies run on-site training for contractors regularly. A "marketing for contractors" add-on seminar at one of their training days gets AOM in front of a captive audience.

G. The "Contractor's Wife" Network

This is the real outside-the-box play. In small to mid-size construction companies (10-50 employees), the owner's spouse often manages the office, the books, and the marketing. They're the ones who know the business needs better social media. They're on Facebook groups, local business women's networks, and they talk to each other.

Finding and engaging with Facebook groups or local meetups where these office managers and business partners gather could be a high-conversion, zero-competition channel. Nobody is marketing to them.

3. Partnership Outreach Templates

Template 1: For Service Providers (CPAs, Insurance, Attorneys, Coaches)

Subject: Quick question about your construction clients

Hi [Name],

I run AOM, a creative production company in Phoenix. We specialize in helping mechanical and HVAC contractors build their brand presence through video, websites, and social media management.

I came across [Firm Name] and noticed you work with a lot of the same contractors we serve. I had a thought:

Your clients trust you with their business decisions. When one of them asks "how do I get more visible" or "how do I stand out from other contractors," you probably don't have a marketing partner to point them to. We could be that partner.

Not looking to sell you anything. Just wondering if it'd be worth a 15-minute call to see if there's a fit for a referral relationship. We'd send clients your way too.

Either way, appreciate what you're building for the construction community here.

Patrik Matheson AOM | aheadofmarket.com

Template 2: For Supply Houses, Equipment Rental, Wrap Shops

Subject: Free offer for your next contractor event

Hi [Name],

I'm Patrik with AOM. We do video production, websites, and social media for mechanical and HVAC contractors in Phoenix.

I saw that [Company] hosts [events/training days/product launches] for contractors. Here's an idea:

We'd love to film your next event at no cost. You get a professional highlight reel to share with your customers. We get to meet some of the contractors in your network. Win-win.

We just wrapped a website and social media build for Ambition Mechanical (one of the Valley's mechanical contractors), so this is the world we live in.

Worth a quick chat?

Patrik Matheson AOM | aheadofmarket.com

Template 3: For Trade Associations

Subject: Member spotlight series idea

Hi [Name],

I run AOM, a production company in Phoenix that works primarily with mechanical and HVAC contractors.

I had an idea for [Association Name]: a member spotlight video series. Short, professional videos featuring your members, their projects, and what sets them apart. You use them in your newsletter, social media, and member communications. Your members get professional video content they'd never produce on their own.

We'd start with one pilot video at no cost to prove the concept. If your members love it, we talk about making it a regular thing.

We just finished a full brand build for Ambition Mechanical (HVAC contractor in the Valley), so this is exactly what we do.

Would you be open to a conversation about it?

Patrik Matheson AOM | aheadofmarket.com

4. Recommended Industries for Expansion

Beyond construction, these industries have the same characteristics (underserved by marketing, relationship-driven, local, have budget):

A. Landscaping and Hardscaping

  • Same supply chain as construction. Same "trades" mentality.
  • Extremely visual work (before/after is gold for social).
  • Underserved by quality marketing. Most have terrible websites.
  • Often known by the same people who know contractors.
  • Arizona-specific: year-round outdoor work = year-round content.

B. Commercial Cleaning and Restoration

  • Fire/water restoration companies operate like contractors (trucks, crews, job sites).
  • They spend heavily on Google Ads but neglect organic/social.
  • Case study from construction transfers directly.

C. Dental Practices and Med Spas

  • Similar spend level ($3-5k/month for marketing).
  • Extremely visual (smile transformations, facility tours).
  • Competitive market in Phoenix = they need differentiation.
  • Already accustomed to paying for marketing.
  • The "old people can read em, young people love em" design standard works perfectly here.

D. Auto Body and Collision Repair

  • Visual work (before/after).
  • Trades mentality. Underserved by quality marketing.
  • Fleet relationships with construction companies (cross-referral potential).
  • Local, relationship-driven, sustainable retainer model.

E. Property Management Companies

  • Manage commercial and residential properties across Phoenix.
  • Need social media, video walkthroughs, tenant communications.
  • Already work with contractors (cross-referral built in).
  • Stable businesses with recurring marketing budgets.

F. Franchise Owners (Service-Based)

  • Franchise owners of service brands (Servpro, 1-800-GOT-JUNK, Two Men and a Truck) often have marketing money but no local execution partner.
  • Corporate gives them templates. They want to stand out locally.
  • Similar personality to construction business owners.

Execution Plan for Jacob

Week 1: CPAs + Bonding Agents (Tier 1A + 1C)

  • Send 5 partnership emails to the CPA firms listed above
  • Send 3 emails to bonding agents
  • Follow up on LinkedIn within 24 hours of each email

Week 2: Business Coaches + Supply Houses (Tier 1B + 2D)

  • Send 3 emails to business coaches
  • Visit 2 supply houses in person (Arizona Climate Supply + Johnstone Supply Phoenix)

Week 3: Wrap Shops + Staffing Agencies (Tier 2F + 2E)

  • Send 3-4 emails to vehicle wrap shops
  • Send 2-3 emails to staffing agencies
  • Visit 1st Impressions Truck Lettering in person (Central Phoenix)

Week 4: Trade Associations + Attorneys (Tier 3G + 3H)

  • Send association partnership proposals (MTCAZ first, then ABA)
  • Send 2-3 emails to construction attorneys

Ongoing:

  • Podcast guest pitches (Building Arizona, AZ ROC Talk)
  • ROC licensing school partnership (AZCLC)
  • Track every partnership conversation in a simple spreadsheet

Success Metrics

  • 5 partnership meetings booked in first 30 days
  • 2 active referral relationships established in 60 days
  • 1 supply house or association event filmed in 60 days
  • 3 warm leads generated from partnerships in 90 days

Key Insight

The contractors AOM wants to reach already have a circle of trusted advisors: their CPA, their bonding agent, their insurance broker, their coach, their attorney. These people see the contractor's growth, their revenue, their ambitions. They're asked for recommendations all the time.

AOM doesn't need to convince 100 contractors that marketing matters. AOM needs to convince 10 trusted advisors to say "call AOM" when the question comes up. That's the leverage play.

Cold email says "trust me." Partnership says "your CPA sent me."

That's the difference.
